question: What is the main idea behind interdisciplinary collaboration in healthcare?

options.A: Hospital management handling budgets without input from clinicians
options.B: Doctors making all patient care decisions without consulting others
options.C: Nurses working entirely independently within their specific wards
options.D: Professionals from different health fields working together for a patient

explanation: You've got this! Interdisciplinary collaboration simply means bringing different health experts together to combine their unique skills for the best patient outcome. [learn more](GST321_U7_T3#GST321_U7_T3_h1)

question: Why do public health workers look beyond the hospital clinic to address community health?

options.A: Government policies prevent nurses from treating patients alone
options.B: Health sectors cannot function without direct financial profits
options.C: Doctors require assistance from construction workers inside the wards
options.D: Factors outside the clinic like housing and sanitation heavily influence health

explanation: Spot on! Good health isn't just about hospital care; clean water, housing, and food play a massive role in keeping people well. [learn more](GST321_U7_T3#GST321_U7_T3_h1)

question: What makes an interdisciplinary team different from a basic multidisciplinary team?

options.A: Interdisciplinary teams feature active communication and shared decision-making
options.B: Multidisciplinary teams always include community leaders and agriculture workers
options.C: Interdisciplinary teams restrict nurses from speaking during patient rounds
options.D: Multidisciplinary teams rely entirely on a single healthcare provider

explanation: Great thinking! While multidisciplinary teams work side-by-side, true interdisciplinary teams communicate closely and build care plans together. [learn more](GST321_U7_T3#GST321_U7_T3_h2)

question: A patient is recovering from a stroke and needs help with walking and swallowing. Who should be on this care team?

options.A: The pharmacist and the hospital security personnel only
options.B: Only the patient's family members making independent choices
options.C: The nurse, physiotherapist, speech therapist, and the patient
options.D: Only the attending physician and the hospital accountant

explanation: Exactly! Recovery takes a village—different specialists are needed to tackle different physical challenges alongside the patient. [learn more](GST321_U7_T3#GST321_U7_T3_h2)

question: How can partnering with farmers and the agricultural sector help improve community health?

options.A: It provides direct medical treatment for infectious diseases inside farms
options.B: It helps combat malnutrition by improving local food production
options.C: It replaces the need for primary healthcare clinics entirely
options.D: It trains farmers to perform minor surgical procedures in villages

explanation: Well done! Agriculture directly affects food security, which is key to preventing malnutrition in our communities. [learn more](GST321_U7_T3#GST321_U7_T3_h3)

question: Which of these is a great example of working with another sector to stop the spread of infections like cholera?

options.A: Hospital pharmacists reviewing drug expiration dates in the dispensary
options.B: Doctors prescribing antibiotics in a private clinic setting
options.C: A head nurse holding a closed meeting with junior nursing students
options.D: Working with public works to ensure clean water supply to prevent cholera

explanation: Spot on! Teaming up with public works to fix water infrastructure stops waterborne diseases right at the source. [learn more](GST321_U7_T3#GST321_U7_T3_h3)

question: How does strong teamwork help protect nurses from burnout?

options.A: Nurses are excused from direct bedside patient care duties
options.B: Hospital administrations eliminate all night shifts and weekend work
options.C: The heavy mental load of complex patient management is shared
options.D: Doctors take over all charting and documentation responsibilities

explanation: You got it! When the team shares responsibilities and talks things through, the heavy stress of patient care feels much lighter. [learn more](GST321_U7_T3#GST321_U7_T3_h4)

question: Why is the nurse's voice so important in a collaborative healthcare team?

options.A: Nurses hold sole legal authority over all hospital budget allocations
options.B: Nurses are the only professionals trained to diagnose chronic illnesses
options.C: Nurses dictate the operational hours of every hospital department
options.D: Nurses spend the most time at the bedside observing patients

explanation: Exactly! Because nurses are right there at the bedside day and night, they spot subtle changes in patients before anyone else does. [learn more](GST321_U7_T3#GST321_U7_T3_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a common challenge facing healthcare collaboration in Nigeria?

options.A: Abundant medical supplies and excessive staffing levels
options.B: Inadequate infrastructure and fragmented record-keeping systems
options.C: Deep-seated professional hierarchies and historical power imbalances
options.D: Inter-professional rivalry between different healthcare worker groups

explanation: Correct! Nigeria's healthcare system unfortunately battles with shortages, not an excess of staff or medical supplies. [learn more](GST321_U7_T3#GST321_U7_T3_h5)

question: How do strict professional hierarchies sometimes hurt patient care?

options.A: They discourage junior staff and nurses from sharing critical patient observations
options.B: They ensure that every single medication is administered twice as fast
options.C: They eliminate all forms of communication errors between departments
options.D: They force patients to pay less money for hospital admission fees

explanation: Spot on! When junior staff or nurses feel intimidated by strict ranks, they might hold back life-saving observations out of fear. [learn more](GST321_U7_T3#GST321_U7_T3_h5)

question: What does the acronym SBAR stand for in clinical communication?
explanation: SBAR is a standardized communication tool used to structure critical information exchanges between healthcare workers. [learn more](GST321_U7_T3#GST321_U7_T3_h6)

question: A nurse notices a patient's blood pressure dropping fast and calls the doctor using SBAR. What should go into the 'Recommendation' part?

options.A: Asking the doctor to come evaluate the patient or adjust medications
options.B: Listing the patient's full name, age, and home address in the ward
options.C: Describing the nursing school the nurse graduated from last year
options.D: Explaining the weather conditions outside the hospital building

explanation: Brilliant! The recommendation is your professional suggestion on what the team needs to do right now for the patient. [learn more](GST321_U7_T3#GST321_U7_T3_h6)
